response.content:
## Cloud and Data Centre Companies That Entered the Norwegian Market in 2026

Norway's data centre sector saw a wave of new entrants and major expansions in 2026, driven by AI infrastructure demand and the country's abundant hydroelectric power. Below are the key companies that entered or significantly expanded into the Norwegian market during 2026:

### New Market Entrants

- **Volta Infra Holdings** — Founded in January 2026, Volta entered Norway through a landmark $4.7 billion, 16-year colocation lease at the Tydal data centre campus (operated by Bitdeer). The facility will deliver 121 MW of IT capacity powered by hydroelectric energy and equipped with Nvidia Vera Rubin chips. Anthropic is reported to be the end customer under a $10 billion, six-year compute deal.

- **Bitdeer Technologies** — Established its Norwegian presence through its subsidiary Tydal Data Center AS, signing the colocation lease with Volta and managing the Tydal campus infrastructure. Phase I delivery is targeted for end of 2026, Phase II for Q1 2027.

- **atNorth** — The Icelandic/Nordic high-density colocation provider expanded into Norway in 2026, acquiring land for its flagship NOR01 data centre campus at Haugaland Business Park (a 36-hectare site). In June 2026, atNorth joined the Norwegian Data Center Industry association following this expansion.

- **Crusoe** — The AI cloud company entered Norway through a partnership with Polar Data Centers. Crusoe's AI infrastructure is now live at Polar's DRA01 facility in Tørdal, Norway, powering Crusoe Cloud. In October 2026, the partnership expanded with a new 40 MW AI infrastructure development (DRA02).

- **VivoPower** — The Nasdaq-listed company pivoted into Norwegian data centre infrastructure in 2026, starting construction on a 42 MW data centre at Mo i Rana, Norway (announced October 2026).

- **T1 Energy** — Received Norway rezoning approval for a data centre project in 2026.

### Major Expansions by Existing Players

- **Nscale** — Significantly expanded its Norwegian footprint, growing the Narvik campus to 230 MW for Microsoft (with 30,000+ Nvidia Rubin GPUs due in 2027). Nscale secured $790 million in financing from Nordic banks for the Narvik build-out. Microsoft took over the capacity originally planned for OpenAI under the "Stargate Norway" project.

- **Microsoft** — Announced a new data centre region in Sandnes, Norway (July 2026), in addition to taking over the Nscale Narvik capacity.

- **TikTok / ByteDance** — Completed its Project Clover build-out, with all three data centre buildings at Green Mountain's OSL2-Hamar campus now operational (150 MW total), as part of a €12 billion European data sovereignty initiative.

### Regulatory Context

As of November 9, 2026, Norway's government temporarily halted new grid connection reservations for data centres (effective until at least August 2027) and announced plans for a licensing scheme to prioritise facilities serving defence, health, and critical infrastructure. Data centres accounted for 75% of the 26,000 MW in new grid connection applications received by Statnett in 2026. Foreign companies own more than 90% of Norway's data centre capacity.

Seeks to limit rapid buildout while regulation catches up

The Norwegian government has temporarily halted the reservation of connections for new data centers.

The move effectively acts as a moratorium on new grid-connected data center developments until regulations are in place. Projects already connected or already grid-approved are unaffected.

System operator Statnett AS said that the halt is expected to be lifted no later than Aug. 1, 2027.

“We want data centers in Norway, but we can’t have all types of data centers,” Digitalization Minister Torgeir Micaelsen said.

“We must therefore control the growth and ensure that Norway gets the data centers we actually need — those that provide the greatest societal benefit.”
